title: Clean body, clean place
hook: wudu, clean clothes, a clean spot, and the idea behind them

segments.voice: Yesterday: niyyah, the intention, the prayer that begins in the heart before the tongue. Your line was mean it first. Did you catch yourself pausing before you started something? Day ninety-eight.

Look back at this week for a second. A small band crossing the sea to a just king. A year of grief. A bloody road out of Ta'if. A night journey, a migration, a camel kneeling in Medina. The stories are behind us now, and we've started the practices. Yesterday the prayer began in the heart. Today, before anyone says a word of it, watch what happens at a sink. A man rolls up his sleeves at work, in the restroom, and washes his hands, his mouth, his face, his arms to the elbow, wipes his head, washes his feet. A coworker walks in and looks a little puzzled. He's not being fussy. He's getting ready. Today: the cleanness that comes before the prayer.
screen: `A WEEK OF STORIES, BEHIND US.` → `A SINK AT WORK.` → `HE'S GETTING READY.`

segments.voice: The Arabic word is taharah, purity or cleanness. Books of Islamic law put it ahead of the chapter on prayer, because the prayer isn't valid without it. It has three layers. First, the body. For the daily prayers that usually means wudu, the washing the Qur'an itself describes in Surah al-Ma'idah: wash your faces, and your hands up to the elbows, wipe your heads, and wash your feet up to the ankles. After some things, like sleep or using the toilet, the wudu needs to be renewed. After others, like sex, a full bath is needed, called ghusl. Second, the clothes: clean of things like urine or blood. Third, the place: a clean spot to stand on. That's what a prayer rug is for. It isn't holy in itself. It's just a clean surface you can carry anywhere. And here's the surprising part. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said, in a hadith in Bukhari, that the whole earth had been made for him a place of prayer and a means of purification. A field, a parking lot, the edge of an airport gate. Any clean ground will do. And when there's no water, or water would harm you, there's tayammum: you touch clean earth or dust and wipe your face and hands. The idea behind all of it is in a short hadith in Sahih Muslim: purity is half of faith. Half. Not a rule tacked on to the prayer. Half of the thing itself. Some scholars read it as outside and inside together: the water on the skin, and the turning of the heart it's meant to go with.
screen: `TAHARAH — BEFORE EVERYTHING ELSE.` · `THE BODY, THE CLOTHES, THE PLACE.` · `THE WHOLE EARTH, A PLACE OF PRAYER.` · `PURITY IS HALF OF FAITH.` · then, large: `OUTSIDE AND INSIDE TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: make one clean corner. Find a spot near you, a corner of the floor, a chair, a patch of desk. Clear it. If you have a clean cloth, a towel or a scarf, lay it down flat and smooth it with your hands. Then sit near it, and just look at it for a moment: a small place where nothing is piled up. Breathe slowly. If you've done wudu before, you can notice where the water would go. If you pray, this is the kind of place you'd pray on. The bell holds the time.
Taharah. Cleanness of body, clothes and place, the half of faith that comes before the prayer. Today's word.
Your line: a clean corner. Somewhere in your day, at home or at work, leave one small corner clearer than you found it. The prayer, step by step, starts here. Day ninety-eight.

howItsDone: Before each prayer, Muslims make sure they are in wudu (the ritual washing of face, arms, head and feet), that their clothes are clean, and that they pray on a clean spot, often a prayer rug; with no water, they use tayammum with clean earth.

fork.setup: you need to pray, you're in a field, and there's no water anywhere. what does the tradition say?
options: skip the prayer until you find water
touch clean earth and wipe your face and hands
fork.reveal: tayammum: clean earth stands in for water. the Qur'an allows it, and the hadith says the earth was made a means of purification.

original.note: Arabic: purity, cleanness; the chapter that comes before prayer in books of Islamic law.

trapdoor: what you thought: washing up before prayer, like washing your hands before dinner.
what it means: taharah is cleanness of body, clothes and place, and the prayer isn't valid without it.
what a scholar hears: the hadith "purity is half of faith" (Muslim 223), read as outward washing joined to the inward turning of the heart.

sources.ref: Qur'an 5:6 (the washing before prayer, and tayammum)
Sahih Muslim 223 (purity is half of faith)
Sahih al-Bukhari 335 (the earth made a place of prayer and a means of purification)

notes: Editor review 2026-10-01: cut the unsourced 'first chapter of almost every book of law' and 'many Muslims keep a prayer rug' claims (teach and original note); 'scholars read it' softened to 'some scholars'.
Hadith numbers (Muslim 223, Bukhari 335) cited from memory; please confirm.

Wudu is summarized from 5:6 only (face, arms to elbows, wipe head, feet to ankles); the sunnah steps (hands, mouth, nose, ears) appear in the hook's scene. A Keeper may want the full order spelled out.
What breaks wudu and what requires ghusl is kept deliberately brief; schools differ on details (e.g. touching, bleeding).
